message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.1","text":"I, Clement, am a Roman citizen, and I have been able to live my early life with self-control, because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied with dejection and distress. For a thought about death stayed with me—I do not know where it began—repeatedly reminding me that, once dead, I do not exist and no one will ever remember me, as infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion. I shall be nonexistent, knowing those who do not exist, not knowing, not being known, not having come into being, not coming into being. And has the world ever come into being? Before it came into being, what was there? For if it has always existed, it will also exist; but if it came into being, it will also be dissolved. And after its dissolution, what will there be in turn, unless perhaps silence and oblivion? Perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Ῥωμαίων πολίτης ὢν","chosen":"am a Roman citizen","rationale":"Uses the conventional English description while preserving Clement’s stated civic identity."},{"source_quote":"τὴν πρώτην ἡλικίαν σωφρόνως ζῆσαι","chosen":"live my early life with self-control","rationale":"σωφρόνως denotes restrained or temperate conduct, while πρώτη ἡλικία refers to the earliest period of life."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐννοίας μου ἐκ παιδὸς ἀπασχολούσης τὴν ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐπιθυμίαν","chosen":"because from childhood my thought kept the desire within me occupied","rationale":"Preserves the causal force of the genitive absolute and the image of desire being kept occupied."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἀπείρου χρόνου πάντων τὰ πάντα εἰς λήθην φέροντος","chosen":"as infinite time carries everything belonging to everyone into oblivion","rationale":"Retains both the personification of time and the emphatic πάντων τὰ πάντα."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τάχα ἔσται τι ὃ νῦν νοῆσαι οὐ δυνατόν","chosen":"Perhaps there will be something that cannot now be conceived","rationale":"νοῆσαι concerns mental conception or apprehension, not merely physical perception."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἔσομαι δὲ οὐκ ὤν, οὐκ ὄντας εἰδώς","issue":"The supplied masculine plural οὐκ ὄντας has no explicit antecedent. It can be construed as the object of εἰδώς, yielding the unusual sense “knowing those who do not exist,” but the intended relation to the surrounding catalogue of nonexistence remains uncertain.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"1.2","text":"Constantly pondering these and similar things—I do not know from where—I had such painful grief that I grew pale and wasted away. Worst of all, if I ever resolved to thrust the concern away as useless, the affliction became all the more acute for me. I was distressed at this, not knowing that I had a beautiful thought as a housemate, one that would become for me the cause of a good immortality, as I later learned by experience and thanked God, the Master of all. For by the thought that distressed me at first, I was compelled to come to the investigation and discovery of realities; and then I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of pronouncing blessed.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀπαύστως ἐνθυμούμενος","chosen":"constantly pondering","rationale":"Conveys both the uninterrupted recurrence and the inwardly reflective character of ἐνθυμέομαι."},{"source_quote":"ἀκμαιότερόν μοι μᾶλλον τὸ πάθος ἐγίνετο","chosen":"the affliction became all the more acute for me","rationale":"ἀκμαιότερον describes the condition as growing stronger or more intense."},{"source_quote":"σύνοικον καλὴν ἔχων ἔννοιαν","chosen":"I had a beautiful thought as a housemate","rationale":"Preserves the domestic image of the thought dwelling together with Clement."},{"source_quote":"ἀθανασίας ἀγαθῆς αἰτίαν","chosen":"the cause of a good immortality","rationale":"Retains the explicit qualification ἀγαθῆς, which may distinguish beneficial immortality from an enduring state of punishment."},{"source_quote":"ἐταλάνιζον οὓς τὴν ἀρχὴν διὰ ἄγνοιαν μακαρίζειν ἐκινδύνευον","chosen":"I pronounced wretched those whom at first, through ignorance, I had been in danger of pronouncing blessed","rationale":"Preserves the deliberate opposition between ταλανίζω and μακαρίζω."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.3","text":"From childhood, then, while occupied with such thoughts, I frequented the philosophers’ schools in order to learn something certain. I found nothing else there but doctrines being torn down and built up, disputes and rivalries, techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises. At one time, for example, the position that the soul is immortal prevailed; at another, the position that it is mortal. Whenever an argument that it was immortal prevailed, I rejoiced; but whenever one that it was mortal prevailed, I grieved. Yet I was more disheartened because I was unable to establish either alternative as certain in my own mind. Still, I understood that opinions about the theses are taken as false or true according to those who defend them and do not appear as they actually stand with respect to truth. Having therefore at last recognized that a firm grasp is not attained on the basis of the theses being defended, but that opinions are pronounced on the basis of those defending them, and reeling still more amid these matters, I groaned from the depth of my soul. For I was neither able to establish anything as certain, nor could I shake off concern for such matters, although I wanted to, as I said earlier; for when I kept ordering myself to be still, I do not know how, the thought of such things would enter me unnoticed and with pleasure.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εἰς τὰς τῶν φιλοσόφων ἐφοίτων διατριβάς","chosen":"I frequented the philosophers’ schools","rationale":"διατριβαί here denotes places or circles of philosophical instruction rather than casual conversation."},{"source_quote":"δογμάτων ἀνασκευὰς καὶ κατασκευὰς","chosen":"doctrines being torn down and built up","rationale":"Preserves the paired constructive and destructive imagery rather than reducing it to generic disagreement."},{"source_quote":"συλλογισμῶν τέχνας καὶ λημμάτων ἐπινοίας","chosen":"techniques of syllogisms, and inventions of premises","rationale":"λήμματα are propositions or premises adopted in argument, while τέχναι emphasizes methodical argumentative techniques."},{"source_quote":"αἱ δόξαι τῶν ὑποθέσεων παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας ψευδεῖς ἢ ἀληθεῖς ὑπολαμβάνονται","chosen":"opinions about the theses are taken as false or true according to those who defend them","rationale":"παρὰ τοὺς ἐκδικοῦντας makes the advocates, rather than the intrinsic merits of the theses, the basis of the assessment."},{"source_quote":"οὐ παρὰ τὰς ἐκδικουμένας ὑποθέσεις ἡ κατάληψις γίνεται","chosen":"a firm grasp is not attained on the basis of the theses being defended","rationale":"κατάληψις is used in a philosophical context for apprehension or secure cognitive grasp."},{"source_quote":"λανθανόντως μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς ὁ τῶν τοιούτων μοι εἰσήρχετο λογισμός","chosen":"the thought of such things would enter me unnoticed and with pleasure","rationale":"Keeps both the stealth conveyed by λανθανόντως and the expressly pleasurable quality conveyed by μεθ᾽ ἡδονῆς."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.4","text":"Again, at a loss, I said to myself, “Why am I laboring in vain? The matter is clear: if, once dead, I do not exist, it is not fitting for me to grieve while I now exist. Therefore I will reserve grieving for that time, when, since I will not exist, I will not grieve. But if, after all, I do exist in some way, then my grieving now is superfluous.” Immediately after this, another thought entered me, for I said, “What if, indeed, because I have not lived devoutly, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now, and according to the accounts of certain philosophers I shall be handed over to Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus, like Sisyphus or Tityus or Ixion or Tantalus, and shall be in Hades, punished for all time?” Again I countered, saying, “But these things are not real.” And again I said, “But what if they are? Since the matter is uncertain, then, it is safer for me to live devoutly instead. Yet how will I be able, for the sake of what is right, while looking toward an uncertain hope, to master the pleasures of the body? But I have not even been fully assured of what exactly is right and pleasing to God; nor do I know whether the soul is immortal or mortal, nor what reliable account can be found, nor am I able to rest from such thoughts.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Τί ματαιοπονῶ;","chosen":"Why am I laboring in vain?","rationale":"Preserves the image of expending effort fruitlessly."},{"source_quote":"τηρήσω τὸ λυπεῖσθαι εἰς τὴν τότε","chosen":"I will reserve grieving for that time","rationale":"Treats τὴν τότε as an elliptical expression for the future time under discussion without supplying it as Greek text."},{"source_quote":"εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα εἰμί τι","chosen":"if, after all, I do exist in some way","rationale":"Retains the deliberately indefinite τι while expressing the implied question of existence after death."},{"source_quote":"Εἰ μήτι γε τοῦ νῦν με λυποῦντος ἐκεῖ χεῖρον παθεῖν ἔχω","chosen":"What if, indeed, I am to suffer there something worse than what troubles me now","rationale":"Renders εἰ μήτι γε as an apprehensive possibility arising against Clement’s preceding reassurance."},{"source_quote":"Πυριφλεγέθοντι καὶ Ταρτάρῳ","chosen":"Pyriphlegethon and Tartarus","rationale":"Transliterates the named mythological places rather than replacing them with generalized terms."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ᾅδου τὸν αἰῶνα κολαζόμενος","chosen":"in Hades, punished for all time","rationale":"The accusative duration τὸν αἰῶνα presents the punishment as indefinitely or perpetually enduring."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δικαίου χάριν","chosen":"for the sake of what is right","rationale":"The substantivized neuter refers to right conduct rather than necessarily invoking a technical doctrine of righteousness."},{"source_quote":"τίς λόγος βέβαιος εὑρίσκεται","chosen":"what reliable account can be found","rationale":"λόγος may denote an argument or account here; “account” leaves that scope open while βέβαιος conveys dependability."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
